title: Introduce sensitivity-aware residency adapter, RBAC decision prioritizer and KMS chained-fallback audit funnel
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Adds a residency-aware RBAC adapter that propagates sensitivity labels, prioritizes RBAC rules by geozone and sensitivity, introduces a chained KMS fallback for region pinning, and reduces audit noise with a compressed audit funnel. Backwards compatible; rollout via canary.
description: Context: Several enterprise customers require stronger guarantees when requests cross geozones: enforce RBAC decisions based on declared sensitivity labels, ensure KMS usage honors region pinning with a tolerant fallback path, and avoid overwhelming audit pipelines with noisy telemetry. Motivation: Close gaps found during a recent compliance review (SUP-1820) where operator-scoped requests were permitted despite mismatched residency claims and audit traffic caused high ingestion costs. What this PR changes: 1) residency-adapter: a new sensitivity-aware RBAC adapter that enriches incoming operator/service claims with a derived sensitivity label and uses a decision-priority matrix to evaluate RBAC v2 rules. 2) kms/fallback: a chained KMS selector that attempts region-local CMK, then geo-fallback CMK in same legal zone, then a tenant-consent-proxy path; all attempts are recorded in an encrypted audit envelope. 3) audit/compression: lightweight compression and deduplication for repetitive low-entropy audit events, plus a sampling profile per sensitivity tier. 4) decision cache TTL heuristics: TTLs are now informed by sensitivity tier and recent policy changes to reduce cache poisoning risk. Design notes: The adapter is OPA-compatible and exposes a single decision endpoint used by the existing authz flow; policy ordering is explicit and documented in docs/security/residency-rbac.md; KMS selection is pluggable for private deployments. Testing and observability: unit tests, integration harness against a local kms-mock, and a canary that emits metrics to the console dashboard. Rollout plan: Canary 5% traffic on Dedicated for 48 hours with alerting thresholds on decision latency, KMS fallback rate, and audit ingest size; if stable, 25% for 72 hours then full rollout. Rollback steps: feature flag off and clear decision cache; kms calls fall back to previous selector. Security review: threat model completed, no new plaintext secrets, audit envelopes encrypted under tenant CMK where possible. Follow-ups: integrate with Optimize to recommend sensitivity-tagging on prompts and add a UI toggle in Console for residency strictness. See linked Linear ENG-6234 and ENG-6291 for eval prompt sets and migration steps.
